solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bill's singing well

definitions.meaning: a bill is a request for payment sent to a customer
a singer performing at their best is said to be '...', in good vocal form

explanation.surface: Someone praises Bill's fine singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is the trade document; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a bill is the itemised demand for payment a supplier sends.

clue.text: Venus may be infiltrated by a mole

indicators.note: the single letter slips inside the other letters, infiltrating them
the letters may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A spy story: the planet Venus might harbour an undercover agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' looks like a spy, but it is a skin blemish; Venus mixed gives NEVUS before the A goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the medical term for a birthmark or pigmented spot on the skin is a mole.

clue.text: Unfashionable clothing in the suburbs

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
skirts are items of clothing

explanation.surface: Dowdy outfits worn out in suburbia.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the outer districts of a town, away from its centre, are its suburbs.

clue.text: Old city displaced Pole chasing stable home

indicators.note: the anagram follows behind, chasing the other pieces

parts.note: constant means steady, stable
in means at home

indicators.note: the letters are moved out of place into a new order

explanation.surface: A Polish refugee pursuing a secure place to live in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but its letters are rearranged to OPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical fact: Istanbul was formerly known by this name, capital of the Byzantine Empire.

clue.text: Refrain from supporting self- admiration

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
ego is one's sense of self-importance, self-admiration

explanation.surface: Advice to stop backing someone's vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to do without something, abstaining from it, is to refrain from it.

clue.text: Billy or Danny may be Indian

definitions.text: Billy or Danny may be Indian

parts.words: Billy or Danny may be Indian
parts.note: the singer Billy and the ... Eleven heist leader Danny share a surname with the sea that lies south of India

explanation.surface: Two men called Billy and Danny might come from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like nationality, but it is the name of a sea; Billy is the pop singer and Danny the George Clooney character.
explanation.definitionFit: An example trio: one word follows Billy and Danny as a surname and Indian as a body of water.

clue.text: Once pictures start to get legal, leaving little to the imagination

parts.note: ex means formerly, once

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter

parts.note: licit means lawful, legal

explanation.surface: Once photos start being legal, they become racy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'pictures start to' as the first letter of 'pictures'; 'get' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: openly graphic content, especially sexual, is frank and nothing is hidden.

clue.text: Either retiring or extroverted

definitions.meaning: leaving office, as a departing president does
sociable and friendly, the opposite of shy

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether someone is shy or sociable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' tempts as 'shy', the opposite of the other sense, but it means leaving a post.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a departing office-holder, and a sociable, gregarious personality.

clue.text: One in four supporting Swedish top team

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece supporting sits underneath the other
the top of the word is its first letter

parts.note: a quad is a quadruplet, one of four babies born together

explanation.surface: A footballer, one of four, playing for a leading Swedish side.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a group of players, or of police or soldiers, working together is a team.

clue.text: On a diet, perhaps, including those in charge above

indicators.note: the other letters wrap around and include this piece
perhaps shows the letters as only one possible form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: foremen are those in charge of workers

explanation.surface: Dieting, perhaps, even the bosses, as stated above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a diet' is jumbled to ATIONED, which wraps FOREMEN after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something mentioned earlier in a document is referred to as the above.

clue.text: Director's short time in quarantine not bad

indicators.note: something gone bad has been spoiled, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: T is the standard short form of time

explanation.surface: A film director spent a brief and not unpleasant spell in quarantine.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Director' stands for 'is'. 'not bad' reads as mild praise, but 'not' is part of the fodder and 'bad' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the American film-maker behind Pulp Fiction is a famous movie director.

clue.text: Bound to enter convenient old cinema

indicators.note: one word is made to go inside the other, entering it

parts.note: fit, as in 'fit for purpose' or 'as you see fit', means suitable or convenient
a bound is a leap or jump

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to go into a handy old picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'obliged', but it is the noun for a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A British colloquialism: a fleapit is a shabby, run-down picture house, supposedly with fleas in the seats.

clue.text: Berserk UK mostly came apart

indicators.note: something come apart has broken up, so the letters are broken and reassembled
most of the word came is used, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: Britain went mad and largely fell to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims 'came' to CAM, which is mixed with UK by 'apart'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: running wild in a frenzy is going berserk, from a Malay word for a frenzied attack.

clue.text: See 11
Neutrois calling for broadcast

parts.note: neutrois is a non-binary gender identity, one under the trans umbrella
a calling, a vocation, is one's mission in life

explanation.surface: Someone's neutral gender identity is their vocation, to be spread abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a radio or TV programme sent out over the airwaves is a broadcast.

clue.text: Last 23 to go round moon

indicators.note: the letters are sent around, mixed into a new order

parts.note: the cross-reference points to the answer of 23 down, meaning the best

explanation.surface: The last of the best people orbiting the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round' suggests orbiting, but it shuffles LAST with the 23-down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a natural body orbiting a planet, such as Earth's companion, is a satellite.

clue.text: They doubt coronavirus's origin in infected bats, ultimately

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: septic means infected by bacteria

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter
the ultimate letter of the word is its last

explanation.surface: A conspiracy angle: people dispute that the pandemic began in diseased bats.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: people who question claims instead of believing them are doubters.

clue.text: Trigger for Spooner is someone experimenting with flagellation

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: flagellation is flogging, to whip
a trier is someone who tries things out

explanation.surface: A kinky experimenter, as the Reverend Spooner might describe them.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of WHIP TRIER to get the spoken answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A function: a hidden wire stretched low that sets off a trap or alarm when touched is a trigger.

clue.text: Filthy rich "saint" fiddled with the tops of innocent teenagers — yes, that's religion!

indicators.note: filthy describes something dirtied and messed up, a hint that the letters are jumbled
something fiddled with has been tampered with and rearranged
the top of each word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tabloid exposé of a wealthy holy man's scandal, ending in mock outrage at faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filthy rich' reads as one phrase meaning very wealthy, but 'rich' is fodder; RICH SAINT with I, T, Y from the first letters of 'innocent teenagers yes' is mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the faith founded on the teaching of Jesus is one of the world's major religions.

clue.text: Cast parts but not the lead

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: factors are parts or elements of a whole

explanation.surface: Casting a play, filling every role but the starring one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' and 'lead' sound theatrical, but 'parts' means components.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the performers in a play or film collectively form its cast.

clue.text: Kind of snake seen in summer

definitions.meaning: the venomous viper common in Britain

explanation.surface: A snake species that turns up in hot weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' reads as the season, but it is one who sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: Britain's venomous viper, and a person or machine that adds up figures.

clue.text: Pages in pioneer recipe for sausage

indicators.note: a recipe mixes ingredients together, so these letters are combined and reordered

explanation.surface: A trailblazing cook's book has pages giving a sausage recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a spicy, dry Italian-American salami often sliced onto pizza is a kind of sausage.

clue.text: Obscene literature includes the best!

indicators.note: the run of words includes the letters wanted within it

explanation.surface: An ironic boast that smut is top-class writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the select top group, the cream, is the pick of a bunch.

clue.text: Spiked, like some shoes

definitions.meaning: a drink spiked has had alcohol or a drug secretly added
shoes fastened with laces threaded through are described this way

explanation.surface: Studded, as some footwear is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spiked' suggests running shoes with spikes, but it is the drink that has been doctored.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a drink doctored with alcohol, and footwear tied up with strings.

clue.text: First link with big man flu uncovered

indicators.note: each word has its covering, its outer letters, stripped away, leaving the inside

explanation.surface: A man's first illness exposed, a dig at 'man flu', the supposed male exaggeration of a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the inner letters of each of the five words: IN, IT, I, A, L.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the opening stage of something, as in an opening payment, is its first one.

clue.text: Contents of Illinois omelettes are nauseating

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit inside these words, as their contents

explanation.surface: The fillings of Midwestern omelettes turn the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something offensive, especially in smell, is foul and sickening.

clue.text: Out of true fondness, Jack and Jane finally got married

indicators.note: the final letter of each of these three words is taken

parts.note: to wed is to get married

explanation.surface: A sincere love story: Jack and Jane at last tied the knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of true fondness' reads as one phrase, but 'Out of true' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something bent or slanted off its proper line is crooked, not straight.

clue.text: Notice lines likely to cause problems

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice
lines of poetry are verse

explanation.surface: A warning that certain written lines could cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: unfavourable conditions or effects are harmful, working against you.
